chunks: I asked him about the man who urinates and nothing (from it) touched his hand — can he immerse it in the water? He (AS) said: 'Yes, even if he was in a state of janabah (sexual impurity).'

key_terms.الْمَاءِ: the water — typically referring to a vessel of water used for ritual purification
key_terms.جُنُباً: janabah — the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl (full ritual bath), typically resulting from sexual intercourse or ejaculation
key_terms.يَغْمِسُهَا: to immerse/dip (the hand) — the act of putting the hand into a vessel of water before washing

ai.seo_question: Can a man who urinated but whose hand was untouched put his hand in water according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Muhammad ibn Muslim addresses a practical question about ritual purity: if a man urinates but his hand remains clean (untouched by urine), he is permitted to immerse his hand directly into water — even if he is simultaneously in a state of janabah. The ruling indicates that the prohibition on immersing impure hands applies only when the hand has actually been contaminated. The ruling reflects a foundational principle in Shia fiqh that ritual impurity (najasah) is specific and traceable — the absence of contact with a najis substance means there is no impurity on the hand, regardless of one's broader state of major ritual impurity (janabah).
word_analysis: in a state of sexual impurity (janabah)
